perspective:
Brandon has access to the following information:

- He is Brandon Talayumptewa, an insurance agent. He meets Benjamin Erickson in a professional setting because Benjamin is seeking business insurance advice.
- In the first meeting, Brandon is aware/believes Benjamin has limited formal education and worries about explaining complex insurance clearly. He tells Benjamin that comprehensive coverage involves liabilities and assets. He explains liability insurance as a safety net and gives the example of a slip-and-fall covering legal/medical costs. He explains asset protection as covering inventory and equipment. He hears Benjamin say the terms are new, ask for an example, say the explanation makes sense, ask about assets, and thank him for breaking it down.
- After that interaction, Brandon revises his belief about Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information and feels more confident. In the next meeting, he discusses more complex policy options: business interruption insurance covering income loss when Benjamin cannot operate normally, and property insurance covering damages and theft. He hears Benjamin say he is ready, has been reading up, finds business interruption crucial in unpredictable times, and finds comprehensive coverage reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, Brandon feels insecure that he may be too detail-focused and wants to keep discussions interesting. He hears Benjamin say he appreciates thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. Brandon tells a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars, says it is about assessing unique risks, and compares it to Benjamin’s business but “less unusual.” He hears Benjamin react with fascination and agree.
- Later, pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to his personal anecdotes, Brandon wants to add more value. He asks whether Benjamin has considered strategic investments to lower premiums and suggests upgrading security systems can protect assets and reduce insurance costs. He hears Benjamin say he is all ears, hasn’t thought of it, calls it a win-win, and agrees to explore it.
- Later, encouraged by their strong rapport and successful collaboration, Brandon feels optimistic about proposing a joint venture. He proposes co-developing a platform that integrates risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. He hears Benjamin agree, ask what he has in mind, call the idea groundbreaking, say combining their expertise could set them apart, and agree to draft initial plans.

Excluded from Brandon’s perspective: Benjamin’s exact education level, personality type, private thoughts, hidden motives, and any events or narrator-only details not stated or observed by Brandon.
